newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin to cut short holiday, return to Moscow.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to cut short holiday, return to Moscow.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin will return to Moscow from his holiday later on Wednesday, the Kremlin press service said, giving no explanation for what appeared to be a sudden change in schedule.
Interfax news agency said last week that Yeltsin was due to stay in the Black sea resort of Sochi until May 4.
Earlier on Wednesday Yeltsin met Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov to discuss tensions in southern Russia near the rebel region of Chechnya, after a series of violent incidents there.
Yeltsin also met First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov in Sochi to discuss a number of decrees to fight corruption and to impose tighter state control on the alcohol market.
The Kremlin initially said that Yeltsin, who left for Sochi on April 18, would take up to 12 days off, breaking the holidays for two days during last week's visit by Chinese President Jiang Zemin.
